title: The Faucet Before the Water
concept: On November 9th the governor announced InvestNorth, a state-sponsored financing platform pitched at data centers, built with Plural of San Francisco on top of Alaska Data Corp, an AIDEA company that AIDEA's board voted $20 million in January. Tokenization is a digital record of who owns a stake. Some deals may be reserved for Alaskans, no offering is open and terms aren't decided, and by the sources reviewed here none names an AI project. The Daily News counts at least seven meetings with Plural's chief executive and a critic calls it public money to Lower 48 corporations. AIDEA's board meets again December 4th and on December 7th Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins becomes governor and says he would support a pause on data center construction until there are rules. The film draws all of it as a brass faucet with a face at the end of a pipe with nothing to pour, and ends on a hard cut at a dust speck that does not fall.

fingerprint.palette: overcast pewter-sage sky rising to light straw, wet gravel with puddle glints, far spruce green, brushed brass reserved for Drip, galvanized grey pail, cream notice sheets with slate type, tomato reserved for the Rulebook and circled dates, electric mint reserved for the AI slip
fingerprint.light_story: overcast gravel-lot day, paper-lit cutaways, a hard cut to black
fingerprint.metaphor: a brass faucet at the end of a long pipe with nothing yet to pour, a rulebook always arriving last

palette: overcast pewter-sage sky rising to light straw, wet gravel with puddle glints, far spruce green, brushed brass reserved for Drip, galvanized grey pail, cream notice sheets with slate type, tomato reserved for the Rulebook and circled dates, electric mint reserved for the AI slip
divergence_note: The last films were a lime stake tag on raven dusk (11-12), pink-gold ice fog with amber (11-11), a violet shore with vermilion and lemon (11-10), an oxblood courtroom (11-09) and a permafrost road (11-08). This film is an overcast pewter-sage gravel lot under the Chugach with brushed brass on one hero, tomato red on one binder and mint on one slip, with no lime, no pink-gold and no plum. Its hero is a brass spigot with a face rather than a stake, tag or puck, its device is a pipe in perspective that the camera runs along, its tokenization is a coat check, and it ends on a speck that does not fall. Honest cost: several shots stay on the same lot.

treatment.title: The Faucet Before the Water
treatment.summary: Two of three returned pitches independently reached a faucet or spigot before the water, because the angle is about order, not a verdict. A personified fixture with a want and nothing to pour is a neutral hero that implies no AI project the sources never name. The calendar gives the film a clock the viewer can check. The Test keeps the critic's card held unjoked. Showrunner synthesis, the scorer step was skipped because the pitches converged.

angle.thesis: Alaska built the money pipe before there was anything to pour through it, and the live question isn't build versus pause, it's order: do the rules come first, or the money?
supporting_facts: AIDEA owns Alaska Data Corp and its board voted it $20 million, yet no offering is open and terms aren't decided (c3, c5, c9, c10).
By our read of the sources reviewed, none names an AI project or customer. AI is the pitch, from Plural's CEO (c14, c15).
Dunleavy says do it right (c13). Kreiss-Tomkins would support a pause until comprehensive rules (c16, c17). Both are arguing about rules.
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: The Daily News counts at least seven meetings with Plural's CEO, the board meets again December 4th, and critic Aubrey Wieber calls it public money moving to Lower 48 corporations (c12, c18, c19). That gets its own scene at full strength. The reply is that nothing locked exists yet, and the residents-only option (c8, may) is the real Alaska-first upside, if it is written down.
angle.falsifier: False if, before December 7th, an offering opens, terms are set, or an AI project or customer is named, or if the December 4th board adds money (c9, c10, c15, c18).
runner_ups: Ownership plumbing outlasts the handover (contrarian): folded in as the Alaska-first upside, not the thesis.
Enthusiast conditional win: folded into the turn.
Dunleavy versus Kreiss-Tomkins build versus pause: rejected as the binary all three analysts say misses the story.
guardrails: at least one more meeting on December 4th, never final (c18)
c15 is our read of the sources reviewed
attribute c11, c12, c19 to the Daily News, c19 as the critic's view
no Brefczynski quote, no crypto price or yield claims, no AI project claim
the three analysts converged, so the cross-challenge was the guardrail pass

hook.frame1: A brass spigot with a face stands at the end of a long pipe on a frozen lot, lifts its handle like a brow and coughs one puff of dust.
hook.headline: ALASKA BUILT THE FAUCET FIRST
hook.loopback: Frame 1 is Drip coughing dust at the end of the pipe, the last frame is Drip with a padlock key at his feet and a speck hanging on his lip that does not fall, then a hard cut to black.

open_loop.what: What will come out of the faucet first, rules or money? Planted as a speck that hangs on the lip, paid when the speck hangs again after rules first or money first and the frame cuts to black.

open_loop_2.what: Does MAY become IS? Planted as a flickering neon MAY on the residents-only window, paid when the plank tag says until comprehensive rules, so the word stays a may until someone writes it down.
